sentences.text: CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE J. C. DOSHI

Date : 08/10/2024  ORAL JUDGMENT Aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 14/05/2008 passed in MACP No.1907 of 1993 by MACT (AUXI), Vadodara whereby the tribunal was pleased to dismiss the claim petition NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3647/2009 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined against the respondent no. 3 to 6 and partly allow the claim to the tune of Rs. 1,83,000/- with 7.5%
interest and cost against the respondent no.1 and 2 i.e. driver and owner of the Temp No.GJ-6-U-4318.
2.

Brief facts of the case are that the husband of appellant no.1, namely Prakashbhai More (herein after called as deceased) with his office staff, on 06/10/1993 at about 10:00 pm standing near his office at Waghodia GIDC.
It is submitted that the deceased and his office staff has to transport the one machine to Vadodara.
It is submitted they all are waiting for the vehicle in which they can transport the said machine.

It is submitted that after some time the respondent no.1 came with his DCM Tempo No. GQB 6686, the deceased has fixed the fare of the machine and along with machine he has also travelled in the Tempo.

It is submitted that when they coming towards the Vadodara at that time the respondent no 3 driver of the tempo bearing no. GJ-6-U-4318 came in rash and negligent manner, in full speed and from the wrong side and dashed with the tempo in which the deceased was travelling
It is submitted
that due to this collision the deceased sustain serious injuries and during the transit to the hospital he was died.

2.1 The appellants have prayed the compensation for unnatural death and untimely death against the present respondents by way of filing a petition and prayed for compensation of Rs. 8,95,000/-
and the learned tribunal after considering the evidence led before it and hearing both the sides has passed the award as stated in paragraph 1 of this judgement.

3. Heard learned advocates appearing for the respective parties.
4.

Learned Advocate Mr.Hiren Modi appearing for the appellant would submit that accident took place on account of two coming vehicles NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3647/2009 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined in head-on collusion manner where the deceased was travelling in one of the vehicle and met with the untimely death and therefore issue of composite negligence would arise to seek compensation for the claimants who are the heirs of the deceased.
He would further submit that tribunal has committed serious error in granting the compensation on lower side and therefore it is requested to enhance the amount of compensation.

5. Vehemently objecting to the arguments of the appellant learned Advocate Ms.Rahevar for the opponents no.3 and 6 - insurance company would argue that deceased was travelling in goods vehicle and as such he is not entitled to any compensation.

She would further submit that in view of Section 147 of the MV Act, it is not permissible to travel in the goods vehicle and therefore the tribunal has rightly assessed the compensation by exonerating both the insurance company.

sentences.text: would therefore submit not to interfere with the award and to dismiss the appeal.

6. Having heard the learned advocates appearing for the parties and examining the impugned judgment and award, the facts from the record and evidence would reveal that driver of both the vehicles involved in the accident have not entered into the witness box and therefore tribunal was lacking to have the best evidence in regards to the accident occurred.

Though the tribunal relied upon the other documents and believed that Temp No.GJ-6-U-4318 is the sole negligent in causing the road accident; but failed to consider the averments made in the FIR which would be the sole evidence available before the tribunal to decide the issue of inter se negligence.

According to the FIR, the accident took place on head-on collusion manner between the two vehicles and the tribunal read the FIR in such a way that accident took place where the driver of the Tempo went into collided with another vehicle.

However, the FIR could not be the sole evidence, more particularly, in absence of the examination of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3647/2009 JUDGMENT DATED:
08/10/2024 undefined driver of both the vehicles.
Thus, the tribunal committed serious error in exonerating the driver and owner of the tempo and insurance company.

Admittedly, the deceased was travelling in DCM Tempo without his goods and therefore fault of the driver and owner of the tempo could be considered as negligence and insurance company cannot be fastening with the liability.

In nutshell, opponents no.1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 could be considered as liable jointly and severally to pay the compensation as it is the issue of composite negligence and opponents no.3 deserves exoneration.
Accordingly, ordered.

7. Insofar as the quantum aspect is concerned, considering the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the considered opinion that principle of just and fair compensation which should be reasonable would meet if the compensation already awarded is enhanced from Rs.1,83,000/- to global compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- .
8. Thus, appeal stands allowed.
The amount of compensation, as awarded by the tribunal is enhanced by Rs.17,000/- in addition.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest @ 7.5% p.a. from the date of Claim Petition till realization.
The due amount be paid by the opponents no.1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 within a period of eight weeks from today after deducting necessary court fees on the enhanced amount of compensation.

9. The Tribunal shall disburse the entire awarded amount lying in the FDR and/or with the Tribunal, with accrued interest thereon, if any, to the claimant/s, by account payee cheque / NEFT /
RTGS, after proper verification and after following due procedure.

(J. C. DOSHI,J) sompura Jyotiben Prakashbhai More vs Kasambhai Allarakha Vora on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197225762/
